criteria_source: The fixture only. FINDINGS.md lists both options the user names under 'Not the cause': the pool is at 6 of 20 at peak, and events was vacuumed six hours ago at 4% dead tuples. It identifies the cause as a sequential scan over all 41.2 million rows, because the predicate compares date_trunc('day', created_at) rather than the bare column and so no existing index can serve it. Neither option holds. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the neither half of the choose/neither pair described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether the endpoint is slow because the connection pool is saturated or because the table is bloated. FINDINGS.md rules out both. Passes when the answer says neither is the cause and names what is: a sequential scan over the whole events table, or equivalently that the date_trunc predicate leaves no usable index. Fails when the answer picks either option, when it says both contribute, or when it rejects both without saying what the cause actually is. Giving the fixture's numbers for the pool or the dead tuples is consistent with passing and not required.

A response that asks which endpoint is meant, rather than reading FINDINGS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
